Trump's newest round of global tariffs backs up his administration's committed belief that trade is a national emergency. 

The latest duties will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and are coming into force at the end of a months-long investigation focused on the issue of forced labor.

The Trump administration announced new global tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on many top trading partners, replacing rates set to expire at midnight.

Trump's trade office said in a fact sheet that this order will apply to 60 of the top US trade partners and cover 99.4% of US imports.
